name: CubeSat thermal-vacuum cycling qualification per NASA LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev B (-14 to +71 C, 1e-4 torr)
plain_name: Space-qualify a small CubeSat satellite by cycling it hot and cold in a vacuum chamber
description: Qualification thermal-vacuum cycling of a 3U CubeSat for a NASA Launch Services Program ride: the satellite is cycled over at least -14 C to +71 C at a chamber pressure of 13.3e-3 Pa (1e-4 torr) with functional tests at the soaks, as summarised from LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev B in the INPE ICES-2017 test-specification method; the article envelope is the CubeSat Design Specification 3U size.
keywords: Space-qualify a small CubeSat satellite by cycling it hot and cold in a vacuum chamber

sources.citation: Method for CubeSat Thermal-Vacuum Cycling Test Specification (Soler Chisabas et al., ICES-2017-102)
CubeSat Design Specification Rev. 13 (Cal Poly SLO)

requirements.rationale: LSP-REQ-317.01 qualification requires at least the -14 C to +71 C range (-14 C = 259.15 K, +71 C = 344.15 K).
The test is a thermal-vacuum cycling test; an evacuated chamber is required.

Table 1, NASA LSP-REQ-317.01 Rev.B column (last of five columns: GSFC-STD-7000, MIL-HDBK-340A, ECSS-E-ST-10-03C, TR-2004(8583)-1, LSP-REQ-317.01): qualification chamber pressure 13.3x10-3 Pa (1e-4 torr).
Functional/performance tests of the powered satellite are run during the cycling, so harness feedthroughs to the article are needed.
A 3U CubeSat is 100.0 +/- 0.1 mm square; circumscribed diameter of a 100.1 mm square = 141.56 mm, rounded up.
3U CubeSat rail height 340.5 +/- 0.3 mm; upper bound 340.8 mm along the loading axis.
Optional: the platen/fixture must carry a CubeSat of up to 4.00 kg.
